posts.caption:
Kenya’s public debt reached 69.9% of GDP, with interest payments taking 5.8% according to the World Bank.
More of every tax shilling now pays lenders instead of public services.
Check the national budget debt lines before Parliament votes.
Facts, not financial advice.

scripts.radio:
Good evening, listeners, and welcome to Kenya on Record. Let us examine the numbers that shape our collective future.

Official data reveals Kenya’s public debt has now climbed to 69.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product. But here is the figure that demands our immediate scrutiny: interest payments alone now consume 5.8 percent of our entire national economic output.

To be clear, this is not paying down the actual debt. This is merely servicing the interest. For every one hundred shillings generated across our entire economy—from the mama mboga to large industrial firms—nearly six shillings goes directly toward interest payments. That is capital diverted away from stocking medicine in public dispensaries, repairing neglected road networks, and funding capitation in schools. When debt servicing consumes this much fiscal space, citizens inevitably face higher taxes paired with diminishing public services. Genuine accountability requires us to interrogate borrowing decisions before debt becomes an existential trap.

Kwa ufupi: Deni la taifa sasa limefikia asilimia 69.9 ya pato la taifa, huku riba ya mikopo pekee ikichukua asilimia 5.8 ya uchumi wetu. Pesa zinazopaswa kuboresha hospitali na shule sasa zinaishia kulipa riba ya madeni. Ni haki yetu kuhoji uwazi na manufaa ya mikopo hii.

This is Kenya on Record. Stay informed, stay accountable.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. Here is a critical update from Kenya on Record that every taxpayer should understand.

Our public debt has touched 69.9 percent of GDP. Even more sobering: loan interest payments alone now swallow 5.8 percent of our country's entire economic output.

Think about what that means. Before a single shilling goes toward repaying the original loan, and before funds reach counties for healthcare, water, or basic education, nearly six percent of our total economic production is eaten up just by interest.

This is why budget crunches persist and tax demands keep rising. We cannot simply look away when borrowing compromises our sovereignty and daily livelihoods. Forward this to your local ward and constituency groups. Ask your representatives why debt management is failing our communities. Tuwe macho.

scripts.reels:
Kenya’s public debt has officially hit 69.9 percent of our GDP. 

Even more alarming? Loan interest payments alone now swallow 5.8 percent of our total economic output. 

That does not touch the principal debt—it only services the interest. 

Every shilling surrendered to interest is a shilling stripped from public hospitals, classrooms, and roads. 

Our economy cannot carry this indefinitely. Who authorized the borrowing, and where did the money go?
